note: MOD_PLAN A33 (STRATA_EXPDEC_SWIGLU) and A35 (STRATA_IC_WARM_MB) retest on the CURRENT fast-hip preset (deferral on: STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU=1, STRATA_EXPDEC_DOWN=1, STRATA_POOL_FUSE_PHASES=1); the first run (04-gpu-launches) was n.s. on a base with reclaim hits. Both are exact (same text expected: the text-hash line must say identical for every arm). expdec-swiglu fuses gate/up + SwiGLU + q8_1 into one launch where EXPDEC takes the layout (needs STRATA_EXPDEC=1, a gate/up type of IQ2_XXS/IQ2_XS/IQ3_XXS/IQ3_S/IQ2_S; layers whose gate/up type is IQ1_M keep the old path, and the model has such layers, so expect a partial effect); it works with the deferral. STRATA_IC_WARM_MB does NOT (kern-hip, 2026-11-11): the warm branch is forked only where the fused CPU-row combine runs (verify.cpp: warm_now requires cfuse_on, and cfuse_on requires !defer_), so on the preset it prints its start-up line and then never launches; the earlier ic-warm arms on this base were no-ops. It is therefore measured inside the no-deferral world: read nodefer+ic-warm32/64 against nodefer only (nodefer vs base is the known deferral gain). ic-warm reads the next layer's pre-doorbell weights (mixer projections, router: the engine prints their MiB per layer at start) on a side stream while the combine waits for the CPU rows, to keep them in the 80 MiB Infinity Cache: 32 / 64 = the cap in MiB per layer. Only if it gains >= 2% there is it worth moving the warm fork to the deferral's own wait (post(l)'s heavy-row wait, STRATA_VERIFY_DEFER_CPU_BELOW), a code change. Order: abtest.py --tier screen first (promote >= +2% on a case, none below -3%), then --tier confirm. STRATA_ROUTER_FUSE (A33, second half) is INERT on this preset: bf16_router_publish_arm is only taken when the window has no deferral (verify.cpp: rpub requires !defer_), so it has its own spec, a33-router-fuse-nodefer.json; F9's STRATA_ROUTE_FAST (spec 17, 25-kern-hip) is the router-publish fusion that works with the deferral.
